Container.Name: ConvertBar
Container.Overview:
Batch video conversion with HandBrakeCLI, driven from a browser UI.
Drop files into a watched folder and ConvertBar re-encodes them with the preset you choose, replacing or renaming the originals according to your cleanup settings. Queue, history, progress and settings are all live in the web UI.
IMPORTANT — two Unraid-specific notes:
1. Watched folders should point at a disk or cache share (/mnt/diskN/... or /mnt/cache/...), NOT a /mnt/user user share. /mnt/user is a FUSE overlay (shfs) and does not deliver inotify events reliably, so files dropped there may not be picked up until the container restarts and rescans. Ad-hoc adds through the web file browser work on any path.
2. ConvertBar modifies and deletes source files by design (that is the point — it replaces originals with smaller re-encodes). Give it read/write access only to the media you actually want it to touch, and set Browse Roots to confine the file browser.
This server build deletes replaced files by default rather than moving them to a trash folder; the Settings page can switch that to keeping both files while you evaluate the results. Its Settings page hides the desktop-only options (menu bar, notifications, auto-update, launch at login).
3. Before rolling back to an older image tag, switch the cleanup setting back to Trash or Delete first. An older build does not recognize "keep" and falls back to deleting replaced files, so a routine tag rollback while Keep is active would permanently delete every original on its next batch.
The server runs as PUID:PGID (default 99:100, nobody:users), so re-encoded files land with that ownership instead of root:root. Do not add --user to Extra Parameters — it conflicts with entrypoint hooks such as the Tailscale integration; the container drops privileges itself after start.

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: Port for the ConvertBar web UI.

Config.Name: Config Storage
Config.Description: Holds the SQLite database (queue, history, settings) and the probe cache. Small; keep it on appdata.

Config.Name: Media
Config.Description: Your video library. Must be read/write: ConvertBar writes the re-encoded file next to the source and then removes the file it replaced. For watched folders, prefer a disk or cache path (/mnt/cache/media) over /mnt/user — inotify does not work reliably on user shares.

Config.Name: Auth Token
Config.Description: Token required on every request. Must be at least 16 characters with at least 8 distinct characters, or the container refuses to start. Generate one with: openssl rand -base64 24. After 8 failed attempts from the same source, further attempts are refused with increasing spacing up to 30s — even the correct token, while gated, so wait rather than retrying. A successful login clears it immediately.

Config.Name: Browse Roots
Config.Description: Colon-separated paths the web file browser may navigate. Leave as /media to confine it to your library. Note: the browser opens at the first root, so put your main library first.

Config.Name: Allowed Hosts
Config.Description: Comma-separated hostnames to accept in the Host header, e.g. tower.local or tower. IP addresses always work without this; set it if you reach the UI by name or through a reverse proxy, otherwise those requests are rejected with HTTP 421.

Config.Name: Post-Convert Command
Config.Description: Script or executable to run after each conversion, e.g. /config/hooks/post-convert.sh. Runs with no shell; receives the job as CONVERTBAR_* environment variables plus CONVERTBAR_PAYLOAD (the full JSON). Not configurable through the web UI or the HTTP API — environment-variable-only by design, so an authenticated web-UI user can't turn this into remote code execution.

Config.Name: Queue-Drained Command
Config.Description: Script or executable to run once the queue finishes a true drain (batched, up to 100 jobs per run), e.g. /config/hooks/queue-drained.sh. Same restrictions as Post-Convert Command above.

Config.Name: Disable Auth
Config.Description: Set to 1 to run with no authentication at all. Only for a trusted LAN or behind a reverse proxy that already authenticates. Leave empty when using an Auth Token.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: UID the server runs as. 99 = nobody on Unraid. Leave empty or 0 to run as root.

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: GID the server runs as. 100 = users on Unraid.
